```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
# The benchmark code ships with the package (inst/benchmark). show_code() prints
# one of its labelled sections ("# ---- label ----") as a code block. The code
# is not run here, and it is not in a chunk of this vignette on purpose: it uses
# packages that taxastand does not depend on.
bench_src <- readLines(system.file("benchmark", "benchmark-lib.R", package = "taxastand"))
show_code <- function(label) {
  marks <- grep("^# ---- .* ----$", bench_src)
  start <- grep(sprintf("^# ---- %s ----$", label), bench_src)
  end <- marks[marks > start][1] - 1
  if (is.na(end)) end <- length(bench_src)
  code <- bench_src[(start + 1):end]
  while (length(code) && !nzchar(code[length(code)])) code <- code[-length(code)]
  cat("```r\n", paste(code, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
}
res <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "benchmark-results.rds", package = "taxastand"))
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)
tool_labels <- c(
  taxastand = "taxastand", taxastand_oneoff = "taxastand (one-off)",
  utaxonstand = "U.Taxonstand", worldflora = "WorldFlora", taxify = "taxify"
)
shown <- setdiff(res$tools, "taxastand_oneoff")
# in the speed tables the two ways of using taxastand are told apart
speed_labels <- replace(
  tool_labels, c("taxastand", "taxastand_oneoff"),
  c("taxastand (prepared)", "taxastand (unprepared)")
)
# a metric for one tool and kind of error
val <- function(tool, kind, metric = "recall") {
  a <- res$accuracy[[tool]]
  a[[metric]][a$kind == kind]
}
# seconds to match n queries, formatted
secs <- function(tool, n) {
  s <- res$speed[[tool]]
  x <- s$seconds[s$n_queries == n]
  sprintf(if (x < 1) "%.2f s" else "%.1f s", x)
}
# one column per tool, one row per kind of error
wide <- function(metric) {
  kinds <- res$accuracy[[1]]$kind
  out <- data.frame(kind = kinds, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (tool in shown) {
    a <- res$accuracy[[tool]]
    out[[tool_labels[[tool]]]] <- pct(a[[metric]][match(kinds, a$kind)])
  }
  out
}
```

taxastand is one of several R packages that match scientific names against a
taxonomy. This vignette compares it with three others that do a similar job,
on names with known errors, so that you can judge which suits your data:

- [taxify](https://github.com/gcol33/taxify): matches against backbones that it
  downloads.
- [WorldFlora](https://cran.r-project.org/package=WorldFlora): matches against
  the [World Flora Online (WFO)](https://www.worldfloraonline.org/) backbone.
- [U.Taxonstand](https://github.com/ecoinfor/U.Taxonstand): matches against a
  database that you supply.

### Packages that are not compared

Three other packages resolve names by calling a web service instead of
matching against a local reference:

- [TNRS](https://cran.r-project.org/package=TNRS): the Taxonomic Name
  Resolution Service, which resolves plant names against an online backbone (as of writing, three were available: [WFO](https://www.worldfloraonline.org/), [WCVP](https://powo.science.kew.org/about-wcvp), and [Cactaceae at Caryophyllales.org](https://caryophyllales.org/cdm_dataportal/taxon/b6ec8d50-7f37-4a17-af01-b1fae138c749))
- [rgbif](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rgbif): an interface to the [Global
  Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF)](https://www.gbif.org/), whose `name_backbone()` matches
  names against the GBIF backbone.
- [wfor](https://github.com/worldflora/wfor): resolves plant names against WFO by calling the WFO API.

One of these may be a good choice when you want the current taxonomy of a particular
service and can work online. However, because they are API-based, the same query can
give a different answer once the service updates its taxonomy or its matching,
and the time taken depends on the network and the server, not on the package.
Results can therefore not be reproduced reliably or timed fairly, so they are
left out of this benchmark.

### How the numbers were made

The numbers come from a benchmark that was run once, on the maintainer's
machine, and saved with the package (the packages compared are not
dependencies of taxastand, and taxify needs a large download). All the code
that produced them is [shown below](#code). Please read the
[limits](#limits) before drawing conclusions.

## Benchmark Summary

- On most kinds of error, every package returned the right record for nearly
  every query. The exceptions, in the share of queries for which the right
  record was returned: taxify on a misspelt genus
  (`r pct(val("taxify", "genus_deletion"))`), WorldFlora on short epithets
  (`r pct(val("worldflora", "short_epithet"))`) and U.Taxonstand on homonyms
  (`r pct(val("utaxonstand", "homonym"))`).
- Results differed for homonyms (the same name published by different authors),
  depending on whether packages used the authors. For example, WFO has four
  records named *Linum perenne*, with the authors L., Lam., Vill. and Guss.
  Asked for *Linum perenne* Lam. (checked with only those four records as the
  reference), taxastand returned only that record. WorldFlora returned all four
  records and marked the Lam. one as its best match. Over all of the homonym
  queries, taxastand returned exclusively the right record
  `r pct(val("taxastand", "homonym", "unambiguous"))` of the time,
  U.Taxonstand `r pct(val("utaxonstand", "homonym", "unambiguous"))` and
  WorldFlora `r pct(val("worldflora", "homonym", "unambiguous"))`. WorldFlora's
  best match, which it chooses using the author, was the right record
  `r pct(val("worldflora", "homonym", "pick_precision"))` of the time.
- taxastand found more misspelt genera and misspelt authors than taxify (genus
  typo: `r pct(val("taxastand", "genus_deletion"))` against
  `r pct(val("taxify", "genus_deletion"))`; author typo:
  `r pct(val("taxastand", "author_typo"))` against
  `r pct(val("taxify", "author_typo"))`). U.Taxonstand and WorldFlora were
  slightly better than taxastand on misspelt genera
  (`r pct(val("utaxonstand", "genus_deletion"))` and
  `r pct(val("worldflora", "genus_deletion"))`).
- taxastand does not guess. When several records fit equally well it returns
  all of them, so on names without an author it gives a single answer less
  often than packages that always choose one. Its single answers were right
  every time or nearly so.
- U.Taxonstand and WorldFlora are much slower than taxastand and taxify, which
  are similar to each other. Matching 100 queries (after warm-up) took
  `r secs("taxastand", 100)` with taxastand using a prepared reference,
  `r secs("taxify", 100)` with taxify, `r secs("utaxonstand", 100)` with
  U.Taxonstand and `r secs("worldflora", 100)` with WorldFlora. taxastand
  without a prepared reference took `r secs("taxastand_oneoff", 100)`. See the
  [speed tables](#speed).

## How the comparison works

**The same reference for every package.** Each package is given exactly the
same reference table: the World Flora Online backbone as installed by taxify
(`r format(res$reference_records, big.mark = ",")` species and infraspecific
names). taxify can only use its own backbones, WorldFlora reads WFO, and
taxastand and U.Taxonstand accept any table, so using WFO lets all four run on
identical data and makes the numbers directly comparable.

**Queries with known answers.** Each query is made by damaging a name taken
from the reference, so the correct record is known. There are
`r res$n_per_kind` queries for each kind of damage (fewer where the damage did
not change the name), drawn at random. The query code is in [The code](#code).

```{r, echo = FALSE}
what <- c(
  exact = "Nothing: the full name with its author",
  epithet_substitution = "One letter of the epithet is replaced",
  epithet_deletion = "One letter of the epithet is deleted",
  epithet_swap = "Two neighbouring letters of the epithet are swapped",
  two_edits = "Two letters of the epithet are changed",
  short_epithet = "One letter deleted from an epithet of five letters or fewer",
  genus_deletion = "One letter of the genus is deleted",
  author_punctuation = "Periods removed from the author",
  author_typo = "One letter deleted from the author",
  no_author_exact = "The name without its author",
  no_author_epithet_deletion = "The name without its author, with a letter of the epithet deleted",
  homonym = "A name that several records share, queried with its own author",
  homonym_typo = "The same, with a letter of the epithet deleted"
)
ex <- res$examples[match(names(what), res$examples$kind), ]
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    kind = paste0("`", names(what), "`"), `what changes` = unname(what),
    example = sprintf("%s → %s", ex$original, ex$query),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
)
```

**What is measured.** Every query is scored by record ID:

- *Found*: the right record is among those the package returned.
- *Single answer*: some packages choose one answer for each query: taxify
  always, WorldFlora through `WFO.one()`, U.Taxonstand through its best match.
  taxastand does not guess: it returns every record that fits, and
  its single answer is the record when only one fits. The tables give the share
  of queries that received a single answer, then the share of those answers
  that were right ("answered / right").
- *Speed*: the time to match 1 to 1000 queries.

## Accuracy: Finding the right record

```{r}
knitr::kable(wide("recall"), caption = "Share of queries for which the right record was returned")
```

## Accuracy: Single answers

```{r}
single <- function() {
  kinds <- res$accuracy[[1]]$kind
  out <- data.frame(kind = kinds, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (tool in shown) {
    a <- res$accuracy[[tool]]
    i <- match(kinds, a$kind)
    out[[tool_labels[[tool]]]] <- paste0(
      pct(a$pick_answered[i]), " / ",
      ifelse(is.na(a$pick_precision[i]), "-", pct(a$pick_precision[i]))
    )
  }
  out
}
knitr::kable(single(), caption = "Share of queries that got a single answer / share of those answers that were right")
```

Where a package returns several records, taxastand's result tells you which
queries need a decision. On the author-less typo kind
(`no_author_epithet_deletion`) taxastand returned
`r sprintf("%.1f", val("taxastand", "no_author_epithet_deletion", "mean_hits"))`
records per answered query on average: without an author, many names have
several records that fit equally well, and taxastand reports all of them.

## <a name="speed"></a>Speed

```{r}
speed_table <- function() {
  s <- do.call(rbind, res$speed)
  s$tool <- speed_labels[s$tool]
  w <- reshape(s, idvar = "tool", timevar = "n_queries", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub("seconds\\.", "", names(w))
  rownames(w) <- NULL
  w
}
knitr::kable(
  speed_table(), na = "not run",
  caption = "Seconds to match n queries (best of 3, after warm-up)"
)
```

U.Taxonstand and WorldFlora were timed only up to 100 queries, because larger
runs on a reference of this size take many minutes for those packages.

The "taxastand (prepared)" row are results that used a reference prepared once with `ts_prepare_reference()` and reused for every call. The "taxastand (unprepared)" row are results that passed the reference names (a character vector) to `ts_match_names()`, so the reference is parsed again on every call.

The timings are made after a warm-up: before timing, each package was run once
on the whole set of queries, so one-time costs are not counted. A prepared
reference, for example, is parsed lazily, one genus at a time, so the first time
a genus is used costs more than later calls.

## <a name="limits"></a>Limits of this comparison

- The queries are synthetic and come from one random sample, with about
  `r res$n_per_kind` queries per kind. Differences of a few percent between
  tools are within what a different sample could change.
- Each package was run with its default settings (WorldFlora's
  `acceptedNameUsageID.match = FALSE` and `WFO.one(Auth.dist = ...)` aside; see
  the code below). Settings such as the thresholds for fuzzy matching can be
  changed, and a package tuned to your own data could give different results.
- Only matching was scored. Resolving synonyms to accepted names, which all of
  these packages also do, was not.
- Only plants (WFO) were tested. Results on other groups or on messier
  real-world lists may differ.
- Times are from one computer (`r res$platform`, `r res$r_version`) and will
  differ on yours.
- Versions: `r paste(names(res$versions), res$versions, collapse = ", ")`.
  Benchmark run on `r res$date`.

## <a name="code"></a>The code

This is the code that produced the results above, shown unchanged. It is also
installed with taxastand (`system.file("benchmark", package = "taxastand")`).
The script that runs it, `data-raw/benchmark-vignette.R`, is in the source
repository.

### Reference

The reference is read from taxify's installed backbone, reduced to species and
infraspecific names, and given one row per distinct authored name.

```{r reference, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
show_code("reference")
```

### Queries

`damage()` changes one letter; `make_queries()` builds each kind of query and
records the correct answer.

```{r damage, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
show_code("damage")
```

```{r make-queries, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
show_code("make-queries")
```

### Scoring

```{r scoring, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
show_code("scoring")
```

### One adapter per package

Each adapter builds its package's reference from the shared table and returns
the records matched for a set of queries, plus the package's own single
answer.

```{r adapter-taxastand, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
show_code("adapter-taxastand")
```

```{r adapter-taxify, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
show_code("adapter-taxify")
```

```{r adapter-utaxonstand, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
show_code("adapter-utaxonstand")
```

```{r adapter-worldflora, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
show_code("adapter-worldflora")
```

### Timing

```{r timing, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
show_code("timing")
```

### Running it

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ref <- load_reference("wfo")
queries <- make_queries(ref, n = 100)
adapters <- list(
  taxastand = make_taxastand(ref),
  taxify = make_taxify(ref),
  utaxonstand = make_utaxonstand(ref),
  worldflora = make_worldflora(ref)
)
for (tool in names(adapters)) {
  hits <- adapters[[tool]]$run(queries$query)
  scores <- score_queries(queries, hits)
  print(summarise_scores(scores)) # found, single answer
  print(time_adapter(adapters[[tool]], queries$query)) # speed
}
```
